stages.label: Stage 1: Sound, Compound Roots & Survival
stages.summary: Immediate Austrian & German confidence: clear pronunciation, Lego-style compound root splitting, polite greetings, Kaffeehaus & Beisl basics, and ÖBB transit signs.

stages.label: Stage 2: CEFR A1
stages.summary: Core building blocks: present-tense verb-second (V2) flow, modal verbs, nominative/accusative/dative cases, separable prefixes, hotels, directions, and daily routines.

stages.label: Stage 3: CEFR A2
stages.summary: Practical independence: spoken Perfekt storytelling, two-way prepositions, reflexive verbs, comparative adjectives, healthcare, housing, and subordinate clauses.

stages.label: Stage 4: CEFR B1
stages.summary: Natural social & workplace fluency: relative clauses, Präteritum vs. Perfekt register, passive voice, Konjunktiv II wishes, and Austrian conversational ear-tuning.

stages.label: Stage 5: CEFR B2
stages.summary: Nuanced professional & media command: two-part connectors, genitive prepositions, subjective modals, academic/news argumentation, and regional cultural depth.

stages.label: Stage 6: CEFR C1 (Full Fluency)
stages.summary: Complete native-level mastery: extended participial attributes, Konjunktiv I indirect discourse, Funktionsverbgefüge, Wiener Schmäh & literary prose.

units.title: Austrian Greetings, Kaffeehaus Essentials & Everyday Politeness
units.subtitle: Grüß Gott, Servus, Verlängerter, and navigating Viennese cafés & everyday shops
units.communicativeGoal: Greet locals politely, ask for everyday essentials, order in a Viennese Kaffeehaus, and settle the bill with confidence.
units.grammarFocus: Formal Sie vs. casual du greetings, noun gender articles (der/die/das), Ich hätte gern + accusative, and first compound splits.
units.culturalNote: Viennese Kaffeehäuser serve every coffee with a silver-tray glass of Alpine tap water and never rush guests with an unrequested bill.
units.regionalFocus: Grüß Gott, Auf Wiederschauen, Servus, das Sackerl, der Bankomat, ein Verlängerter, das Schlagobers, and das Beisl.

units.title: ÖBB Rail, Alpine Transit & Compound Word Roots
units.subtitle: Decoding Haupt·bahn·hof, Bahn·steig, and Schienen·ersatz·verkehr across Austria and Germany
units.communicativeGoal: Split long German transit compounds into clear root blocks, buy round-trip rail tickets, reserve seats, and navigate delays.
units.grammarFocus: Right-hand head gender in compounds, directional prefixes (Ein-/Aus-/Um-), separable transit verbs, and weil/obwohl/damit.
units.culturalNote: High-speed ÖBB Railjet and DB ICE networks connect Alpine and urban hubs seamlessly with open platforms and zero ticket turnstiles.
units.regionalFocus: ÖBB Bahnsteig (vs. DB Gleis), hin und retour (vs. hin und zurück), Ruhezone, and Austrian rail announcement phrasing.

units.title: Markets, Bakery Counters, Beisl Menus & Prices
units.subtitle: Semmeln, Erdäpfel, Paradeiser, Naschmarkt weights, and splitting the bill
units.communicativeGoal: Order rolls, produce, and Austrian classics by weight, check allergens, understand euro prices, and split or combine checks.
units.grammarFocus: Measure phrases without von, spoken euro numbers, dative experiencer schmecken, and seasonal adverb heuer.
units.culturalNote: Open-air markets like Vienna's Naschmarkt and neighborhood bakeries anchor daily shopping with fresh regional produce.
units.regionalFocus: Semmel, Erdäpfel, Paradeiser, Jause, Schweinsbraten, Deka (10g deli unit), prickelnd, Kren, Mehlspeisen, and heuer.

units.title: German Sound Craft: Umlauts, ß, ch-Sounds & Austrian Melody
units.subtitle: Crisp ä/ö/ü vowels, ich-Laut vs. ach-Laut, W/V/Z consonants, and soft Viennese cadence
units.communicativeGoal: Pronounce street names, Umlauts, and compound clusters cleanly while tuning your ear to soft Austrian consonants.
units.grammarFocus: Vowel length contrasts, final devoicing vs. southern lenis stops, and word-initial stress on separable vs. inseparable prefixes.
units.culturalNote: Spelling rules distinguish ß after long vowels/diphthongs (Straße, heißen) from ss after short vowels (Gasse, Wasser).
units.regionalFocus: Softer Austrian P/T/K articulation, vocalized -er endings, and -ig pronounced '-ik' in Austria vs. '-ich' in northern Germany.

units.title: Introducing Yourself, Countries, Languages & Sie vs. du
units.subtitle: Sharing where you come from, where you live, and navigating social formality smoothly
units.communicativeGoal: Introduce yourself warmly at events or hotels, talk about languages you speak, and read Sie/du cues accurately.
units.grammarFocus: Present tense of sein, kommen aus, wohnen in, sprechen (e→i vowel change), and W-questions vs. yes/no verb-first questions.
units.culturalNote: Using formal Sie with adults outside your friend circle signals mutual respect rather than coldness.
units.regionalFocus: Austrian academic and professional titles (Frau Magister, Herr Diplom-Ingenieur) and warm 'Ich bin der/die + Name' introductions.

units.title: Numbers to 1,000, Clock Times, Viertel über & Opening Hours
units.subtitle: 24-hour schedules vs. spoken half-past (halb vier = 3:30!) and Austrian quarter-hour conventions
units.communicativeGoal: Avoid the classic 'halb vier' trap, confirm appointment and concert times, and read shop opening plaques.
units.grammarFocus: Ordinal & cardinal numbers, um + clock time, am + weekday, and spoken half/quarter time expressions.
units.culturalNote: In German, 'halb vier' always looks forward to the upcoming hour—meaning halfway TO four (3:30), never 4:30!
units.regionalFocus: Eastern Austrian 'viertel vier' (3:15) and 'dreiviertel vier' (3:45) alongside 'Viertel nach / Viertel vor'.

units.title: Vienna U-Bahn, Trams (die Bim), Buses & City Wayfinding
units.subtitle: Validating KlimaTicket & 24h passes, asking locals for directions, and spatial landmarks
units.communicativeGoal: Navigate trams, metro lines, and historic old-town lanes on foot while understanding left/right/straight-ahead directions.
units.grammarFocus: Imperative Sie forms (Gehen Sie geradeaus, biegen Sie links ab) and contraction prepositions zum/zur.
units.culturalNote: Vienna's Wiener Linien network runs on trust-based proof-of-payment; paper single tickets must be stamped at blue Entwerter boxes.
units.regionalFocus: Die Bim (Viennese tram), Jahreskarte / KlimaTicket Österreich, die Stiege (stairwell/building wing), and ums Eck.

units.title: Alpine Gasthof & Hotel Check-In, Rooms & Breakfast Times
units.subtitle: Checking into city hotels and mountain inns, requesting extra pillows or keys, and Ortstaxe basics
units.communicativeGoal: Complete hotel check-in and check-out smoothly, ask about Wi-Fi and breakfast hours, and resolve small room needs.
units.grammarFocus: Possessive determiners (mein/Ihr/unser), es gibt + accusative, and negation with kein vs. nicht.
units.culturalNote: Family-run Alpine Gasthöfe and Pensionen often include hearty regional breakfast buffets and local transit guest cards.
units.regionalFocus: Der Polster (AT pillow vs. DE das Kissen), die Tuchent (AT down duvet vs. DE Bettdecke), and der Lift (AT elevator vs. DE Aufzug).

units.title: Weather in the Alps, Four Seasons & Packing Smart
units.subtitle: Forecasts from Danube sunshine to Tyrolean Föhn winds, clothing compounds, and small talk
units.communicativeGoal: Check mountain and city weather forecasts, shop for rain or winter layers, and chat naturally about the weather.
units.grammarFocus: Impersonal es expressions (es regnet, es schneit, mir ist kalt), temporal adverbs, and compound clothing nouns.
units.culturalNote: As the German saying goes, 'Es gibt kein schlechtes Wetter, nur falsche Kleidung'—layering (Zwiebellook) rules outdoor life.
units.regionalFocus: Die Haube (AT winter beanie vs. DE die Mütze), das Leiberl (AT T-shirt), and warm Alpine Föhn wind phenomena.

units.title: Emergencies, Pharmacies (Apotheke), Lost Items & Quick Help
units.subtitle: Finding night-duty pharmacies (Nachtdienst), reporting a lost wallet at the Fundamt, and urgent phrases
units.communicativeGoal: Ask for immediate assistance, find an open Apotheke after hours, and report lost passports, phones, or bags.
units.grammarFocus: Modal brauchen / helfen (+ dative), urgent imperatives, and clear descriptive color/material compounds.
units.culturalNote: Drugstores (Drogerien like dm or Bipa) sell toiletries and bandages, while only a red-cross/green-cross Apotheke dispenses medication.
units.regionalFocus: Austrian emergency numbers (Rettung 144, Bergrettung 140, Euro-Notruf 112), Verkühlung (AT cold vs. DE Erkältung), and Bankomat card blocking.

units.title: The Verb-Second (V2) Engine & Daily Life in Vienna and Berlin
units.subtitle: Keeping the conjugated verb anchored at Position 2 when fronting time, place, or objects
units.communicativeGoal: Describe your weekday and weekend routines fluidly without stiff subject-first monotony.
units.grammarFocus: Strict V2 main-clause word order, Time-Manner-Place (TMP) ordering, and stem-vowel-changing verbs (fahren, lesen, sehen).
units.culturalNote: Quiet hours (Nachtruhe and Sunday shop closures—Sonntagsruhe) shape a calm, restorative weekend rhythm across Austria and Germany.
units.regionalFocus: Austrian month & weekday nuances (Jänner in AT vs. Januar in DE; Samstag vs. northern Sonnabend).

units.title: Accusative Case Mastery: Shopping, Gifts & Direct Objects
units.subtitle: Why only masculine der→den / ein→einen changes, plus accusative prepositions (für, ohne, durch, um)
units.communicativeGoal: Buy gifts, groceries, and tickets while handling direct objects and accusative prepositions effortlessly.
units.grammarFocus: Accusative articles & personal pronouns (mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns), plus durch, für, gegen, ohne, um.
units.culturalNote: Bringing flowers (unwrapped before handing over!) or fine chocolates when invited to someone's home is cherished etiquette.
units.regionalFocus: Um + price ('um fünf Euro' in AT vs. 'für fünf Euro' in DE) and Austrian gift favorites like Mozartkugeln and pumpkin-seed treats.

units.title: Modal Verbs in Action: Können, Müssen, Wollen, Dürfen & Möchten
units.subtitle: Building the German sentence bracket (Satzklammer) for plans, rules, permissions, and abilities
units.communicativeGoal: Coordinate plans with friends, understand museum or alpine trail rules, and express wishes politely.
units.grammarFocus: Present-tense conjugation of all six modals + infinitive locked at clause end.
units.culturalNote: Clear signage on trails and public spaces uses 'Bitte nicht...' or infinitival 'Betreten verboten' rather than personal scolding.
units.regionalFocus: Austrian modal favorite 'mögen' in polite questions ('Magst du einen Kaffee?' vs. DE 'Möchtest du einen Kaffee?').

units.title: Separable & Inseparable Prefix Verbs: Unlocking Action Nuance
units.subtitle: Contrasting einkaufen, aufmachen, and anrufen with verstehen, bezahlen, and empfehlen
units.communicativeGoal: Talk about phone calls, grocery runs, opening windows, and getting recommendations with crisp sentence brackets.
units.grammarFocus: Separable prefixes (ab-, an-, auf-, aus-, ein-, mit-, vor-, zu-) vs. inseparable (be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ge-, ver-, zer-).
units.culturalNote: Answering the phone in German-speaking Europe traditionally starts by stating your surname clearly.
units.regionalFocus: Aufsperren / zusperren (AT unlock/lock with a key vs. DE aufschließen / abschließen) and sich ausgehen ('Es geht sich aus!').

units.title: Dative Case Foundations: Recipients, Locations & Mit/Nach/Zu/Aus
units.subtitle: Indirect objects ('giving whom what') and high-frequency dative prepositions (aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu)
units.communicativeGoal: Explain how you commute, how long you've lived or studied somewhere (seit + dative!), and whom you're meeting.
units.grammarFocus: Dative articles (dem/der/dem/den+n), dative pronouns (mir/dir/ihm/ihr/Ihnen), and present tense + seit for ongoing duration.
units.culturalNote: Saying 'Ich lerne seit drei Monaten Deutsch' uses present tense—because you are still learning right now!
units.regionalFocus: Zu Hause / daheim ('Ich bin daheim'—warm Austrian/southern standard for 'at home').

units.title: Family, Friends, Possessives & Describing People
units.subtitle: Talking about relatives, roommates, professions, and masculine/feminine job titles (-in)
units.communicativeGoal: Share stories about your family, partner, or colleagues with accurate possessive endings across cases.
units.grammarFocus: Possessive determiners (sein/ihr/euer—dropping inner -e- in eure!), feminine -in professions, and article omission with jobs.
units.culturalNote: Distinguishing 'ein Freund von mir' ('a male friend of mine') from 'mein Freund' ('my boyfriend') prevents classic misunderstandings!
units.regionalFocus: Austrian kinship warmth: der Bub (AT boy vs. DE der Junge) and das Mädel / Dirndl.

units.title: Apartments, Rooms & Two-Way Prepositions (Wechselpräpositionen)
units.subtitle: Where is it (Wo? = Dative) vs. Where is it going (Wohin? = Accusative) with in, an, auf, über, unter, neben
units.communicativeGoal: Describe apartment layouts, arrange furniture, and place items accurately on tables, walls, and shelves.
units.grammarFocus: Nine Wechselpräpositionen (an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen) and posture pairs stellen/stehen, legen/liegen.
units.culturalNote: German floor numbering counts Erdgeschoss (ground floor) before 1. Stock (first floor upstairs—US second floor!).
units.regionalFocus: Das Vorzimmer (AT entryway/hall vs. DE der Flur), der Kasten (AT wardrobe vs. DE der Schrank), and der Polster.

units.title: Hobbies, Alpine Hiking, Skiing & Weekend Culture
units.subtitle: Expressing preferences with gern / lieber / am liebsten and planning outdoor excursions
units.communicativeGoal: Compare favorite pastimes, plan a hut-to-hut Alpine day hike or museum afternoon, and buy lift or exhibition passes.
units.grammarFocus: Adverbial preference scale (gern → lieber → am liebsten), treffen, and temporal prepositions vor/nach + dative.
units.culturalNote: Alpine clubs (ÖAV / DAV) maintain scenic mountain huts (Almhütten) welcoming hikers of every generation with soup and strudel.
units.regionalFocus: Schifahren / Skifahren, die Almhütte, die Brettljause, and greeting fellow hikers above ~1,000m with 'Servus' or 'Grüß dich'!

units.title: Supermarkets, Deposit Bottles (Pfand) & Everyday Errands
units.subtitle: Weighing produce, bakery self-service tongs, returning Pfand bottles, and post/parcel pick-ups
units.communicativeGoal: Breeze through Austrian and German supermarkets, bakeries, dry cleaners, and parcel lockers.
units.grammarFocus: Packaging & container nouns (eine Packung, eine Flasche, ein Glas), partitive pronouns (welch-/kein-), and imperatives.
units.culturalNote: Shoppers pack their own groceries rapidly at the checkout belt and bring reusable totes—don't block the scanner while bagging!
units.regionalFocus: Billa/Spar Feinkost deli counters (freshly made Semmeln on demand!), das Sackerl, and Austria's 2025+ Einwegpfand return system.

units.title: Concert Halls, Museums, Cinema & Cultural Invitations
units.subtitle: Booking Musikverein or Staatsoper tickets, coordinating meetups, and reacting to performances
units.communicativeGoal: Buy seated or standing-room concert tickets, arrange pre-show drinks, and talk about music, art, and film.
units.grammarFocus: Coordinating conjunctions without inversion (und, aber, oder, denn, sondern) and time-place meetup expressions.
units.culturalNote: World-class Viennese opera and symphony performances offer Stehplätze (standing-room tickets) for just a few euros.
units.regionalFocus: Wiener Staatsoper & Musikverein Stehplatz tradition, Garderobe coat-check rules, and Pausenbuffet spritzers.

units.title: Spoken Past Mastery: Perfekt Across Regular, Irregular & Prefix Verbs
units.subtitle: ge-...-t vs. ge-...-en participles, separable auf·ge·macht, and verbs in -ieren without ge-
units.communicativeGoal: Tell complete, natural stories about last weekend, vacations, and workdays in spoken German.
units.grammarFocus: Systematic past-participle formation (weak, strong, mixed, separable ge-infix, inseparable & -ieren zero-ge-) with haben vs. sein.
units.culturalNote: In everyday spoken conversation from Munich to Vienna, Perfekt carries 95% of past storytelling (except war/hatte/wollte/konnte).
units.regionalFocus: Austrian sein auxiliary with posture verbs: 'ich bin gesessen / gestanden / gelegen' (vs. northern DE haben).

units.title: Simple Past Anchors: War, Hatte & Modal Verbs in Präteritum
units.subtitle: Why native speakers say 'Ich wollte fragen' and 'Es war toll' instead of clunky modal Perfekt
units.communicativeGoal: Blend crisp Präteritum forms of sein, haben, and modals seamlessly into your spoken Perfekt stories.
units.grammarFocus: Präteritum conjugation of sein (war), haben (hatte), and modals (konnte, musste, wollte, durfte, sollte).
units.culturalNote: Mixing war/hatte/konnte with Perfekt action verbs ('Es war kalt, also sind wir ins Café gegangen') is the exact rhythm of native speech.
units.regionalFocus: Even in Vienna—where Präteritum of action verbs sounds bookish aloud—war and wollte/konnte are completely natural.

units.title: Reflexive Verbs: Morning Routines, Relaxation & Reciprocity
units.subtitle: Sich freuen auf vs. über, sich beeilen, sich treffen, and accusative vs. dative mich/mir
units.communicativeGoal: Talk about getting ready, looking forward to trips, remembering names, and catching up with friends.
units.grammarFocus: Accusative reflexive pronouns (mich/dich/sich/uns/euch) vs. dative reflexives when a body-part/clothing object is present ('Ich putze mir die Zähne').
units.culturalNote: 'Ich freue mich auf Freitag' looks forward to what's coming; 'Ich freue mich über dein Geschenk' rejoices over what already arrived!
units.regionalFocus: Sich ausgehen ('Geht sich noch ein Kaffee aus?' = 'Do we still have enough time/room for a coffee?')—Austria's #1 reflexive gem!

units.title: Comparisons, Superlatives & Choosing Hotels, Routes & Gear
units.subtitle: So ... wie, schneller als, am schönsten, and Umlaut shifts in kurz → kürzer → am kürzesten
units.communicativeGoal: Compare train connections, apartments, restaurants, and travel options clearly and persuasively.
units.grammarFocus: Equative (genauso ... wie), comparative (-er + als), superlative (am ...-sten / der ...-ste), and irregular gut/viel/gern.
units.culturalNote: Direct product and transit comparisons favor concrete facts (travel time, quietness, walkability) over hyperbole.
units.regionalFocus: Comparing Austrian Railjet vs. Westbahn private trains and regional Austrian wine & cheese styles.

units.title: Adjective Endings Without Tears: Der, Ein & Zero-Article Patterns
units.subtitle: Why 'ein guter Wein' and 'der gute Wein' follow one logical signal rule
units.communicativeGoal: Use descriptive adjectives before nouns naturally in menus, compliments, shopping, and emails.
units.grammarFocus: Strong, weak, and mixed adjective declension unified under the 'Someone Has to Show the Gender Signal' principle.
units.culturalNote: Regional designations act as uninflected -er adjectives: Wiener Schnitzel, Salzburger Nockerln, Berliner Luft!
units.regionalFocus: Viennese culinary & architectural phrases: ein kleiner Brauner, ein großer Gespritzter, Altbauwohnung.

units.title: Subordinate Connectors II: Wenn, Als, Dass & Indirect W-Questions
units.subtitle: Distinguishing one-time past 'als' from repeated/future 'wenn' and asking polite embedded questions
units.communicativeGoal: Recount childhood or first-arrival memories with als, frame conditions with wenn, and ask polite indirect questions.
units.grammarFocus: Als (single past event) vs. wenn (whenever/if) vs. ob ('whether'), plus verb-final indirect questions ('Wissen Sie, wann...').
units.culturalNote: Wrapping a question inside 'Können Sie mir sagen, ob...' immediately elevates counter and workplace politeness.
units.regionalFocus: Colloquial Austrian 'wie' heard for temporal 'als' in casual speech—recognizing it passively while using 'als' cleanly.

units.title: Doctor's Visits, E-Card / Insurance & Describing Health in Detail
units.subtitle: Booking appointments (Ordination vs. Praxis), explaining symptoms, sick notes, and recovery wishes
units.communicativeGoal: Schedule a medical or dental checkup, describe how long symptoms have lasted, and wish colleagues 'Gute Besserung!'.
units.grammarFocus: Modal sollen for doctor's advice ('Der Arzt sagt, ich soll...'), wehtun + dative, and temporal seit/vor.
units.culturalNote: Public statutory health insurance (ÖGK in Austria, GKV in Germany) covers clinic visits via chip card.
units.regionalFocus: Die Ordination (AT doctor's office vs. DE die Praxis), das Spital (AT hospital vs. DE das Krankenhaus), and Krankenstand.

units.title: Apartment Hunting, WG Interviews & Registering Your Address (Meldezettel)
units.subtitle: Decoding Altbau listings, Kaltmiete vs. Warmmiete/Betriebskosten, and municipal registration
units.communicativeGoal: Read rental ads, ask smart questions at an apartment viewing, and complete statutory address registration.
units.grammarFocus: Dative verbs (gefallen, gehören, passen), floor/area measurements (Quadratmeter), and polite email inquiries.
units.culturalNote: Both Austria (within 3 days via Meldezettel!) and Germany (Anmeldung) require registering a new residential address at the municipal office.
units.regionalFocus: Der Meldezettel, Betriebskosten, Garçonnière (AT studio flat), and Vienna's world-renowned Gemeindebau & Altbau housing.

units.title: Banking, Contracts, Subscriptions & Polite Customer Support
units.subtitle: SEPA direct debits, canceling contracts (kündigen), warranty claims, and formal emails (Sehr geehrte...)
units.communicativeGoal: Write clear customer-service emails, manage mobile or gym contracts, and verify notice periods (Kündigungsfrist).
units.grammarFocus: Infinitive clauses with um ... zu ('in order to') and ohne ... zu, plus formal letter openings and closings (Mit freundlichen Grüßen).
units.culturalNote: Many German and Austrian annual memberships auto-renew unless canceled in writing before the Kündigungsfrist.
units.regionalFocus: Erlagschein / Zahlungsanweisung, FinanzOnline, and Austrian consumer terminology.

units.title: Festivals, Advent Markets, Ball Season & Social Traditions
units.subtitle: Christkindlmarkt, Viennese Ballkultur, Fasching/Karneval, and seasonal greetings across the year
units.communicativeGoal: Join holiday gatherings, toast appropriately (Prost! vs. Zum Wohl!), and wish friends well across seasonal milestones.
units.grammarFocus: Prepositional verbs with da-/wo- compounds (ich freue mich darauf, worauf freust du dich?) and temporal clauses.
units.culturalNote: Eye contact when clinking glasses during 'Prost!' (beer) or 'Zum Wohl!' (wine) is taken seriously—never cross arms in a group toast!
units.regionalFocus: Wiener Christkindlmarkt, Punschstand, Wiener Ballsaison ('Alles Walzer!'), and 'Guten Rutsch!' into the New Year.

units.title: Relative Clauses Across All Cases & Prepositions
units.subtitle: Connecting rich descriptions smoothly ('die Stadt, in der ich lebe' · 'der Kollege, dem ich geholfen habe')
units.communicativeGoal: Describe people, places, and ideas precisely in multi-clause sentences without chopping speech into tiny fragments.
units.grammarFocus: Relative pronouns (der/die/das/denen/dessen/deren) in nominative, accusative, dative, genitive, and after prepositions.
units.culturalNote: Remember: relative pronoun gender/number matches the noun it refers back to, while its CASE comes from its job inside the relative clause!
units.regionalFocus: Describing Austrian UNESCO landmarks from Wachau river terraces to Salzburg's Altstadt and Hallstatt.

units.title: Written Narrative Past: Präteritum in News, Books & Biographies
units.subtitle: Recognizing strong and weak Präteritum (ging, kam, schrieb, entstand) in print and broadcasts
units.communicativeGoal: Read newspaper articles, museum placards, and novels effortlessly and recount historical biographies.
units.grammarFocus: Narrative Präteritum of strong/irregular verbs and Plusquamperfekt (hatte/war + Partizip II) for 'past-before-the-past'.
units.culturalNote: Knowing when to READ Präteritum (novels, Der Standard, Die Zeit) vs. SPEAK Perfekt (dinner table) marks true B1+ maturity.
units.regionalFocus: Reading Austrian quality press (Der Standard, Die Presse, ORF.at) and Habsburg-to-Republic historical timelines.

units.title: Passive Voice: Processes, Recipes, Architecture & Civic Rules
units.subtitle: Action passive (werden + Partizip II) vs. state passive (sein + Partizip II) and impersonal 'Es wird getanzt'
units.communicativeGoal: Explain how dishes are prepared, when buildings were restored, and how workplace or municipal processes run.
units.grammarFocus: Vorgangspassiv across tenses (wird gemacht / wurde gebaut / ist renoviert worden), Zustandspassiv, and passive with modals.
units.culturalNote: Recipes, manuals, and museum plaques rely heavily on passive voice and 'man' to keep focus on the craft or process.
units.regionalFocus: How classic Wiener Schnitzel (veal, souffléed in clarified Butterschmalz!) and Sachertorte are traditionally crafted.

units.title: Konjunktiv II Wishes, Advice & Unreal Conditions
units.subtitle: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte..., An deiner Stelle würde ich..., and past regrets (hätte ... gemacht)
units.communicativeGoal: Give tactful advice, brainstorm hypothetical scenarios, and express wishes or gentle hindsight without lecturing.
units.grammarFocus: Present Konjunktiv II (wäre, hätte, würde + Inf., könnte, sollte) and past counterfactual Konjunktiv II (wäre/hätte + Partizip II).
units.culturalNote: 'An Ihrer/deiner Stelle würde ich...' ('In your shoes I would...') softens advice far better than 'Sie müssen...'.
units.regionalFocus: Warm Austrian subjunctive softening in workplace and everyday counsel.

units.title: Workplace German: Job Applications, Interviews & Team Meetings
units.subtitle: CVs (Lebenslauf), strengths & experience, moderating meetings, and constructive feedback
units.communicativeGoal: Present your professional background clearly, contribute to German-language meetings, and follow up in writing.
units.grammarFocus: Fixed verb-preposition pairs (sich bewerben um, sich beschäftigen mit, beitragen zu, abhängen von) and nominalizations.
units.culturalNote: German and Austrian interviews value concrete examples and verifiable qualifications over exaggerated self-promotion.
units.regionalFocus: Austrian Kollektivvertrag (14 monthly salary payments including Urlaubsgeld & Weihnachtsgeld!) and Arbeiterkammer culture.

units.title: Nuanced Modal Particles: Doch, Ja, Halt, Eben, Mal & Eigentlich
units.subtitle: Decoding the emotional soul of spoken German—turning robotic sentences into idiomatic warmth
units.communicativeGoal: Hear and use unstressed modal particles to soften imperatives, express shared surprise, or signal friendly resignation.
units.grammarFocus: Pragmatic placement of doch, ja, mal, eigentlich, halt, eben, and wohl in middle-field syntax.
units.culturalNote: 'Komm mal kurz her!' sounds friendly and relaxed; 'Komm her!' without 'mal' sounds like barking an order.
units.regionalFocus: Austrian particle trio eh ('Das weißt du eh'), fei (Tyrol/Bavaria), and geh bitte! (affectionate disbelief: 'Oh come on!').

units.title: Austrian Regional Panorama: Vienna, Salzburg, Tyrol, Styria & Vorarlberg
units.subtitle: Ear-tuning across Austria's nine Bundesländer without losing Standard German clarity
units.communicativeGoal: Understand regional pronunciation and vocabulary shifts from Viennese melody to Alpine Tyrolean and Alemannic Vorarlberg.
units.grammarFocus: Diminutive suffixes (-erl, -l, -le), regional diphthongs, and code-switching between dialect coloring and Österreichisches Standarddeutsch.
units.culturalNote: Austria is pluricentric: Österreichisches Wörterbuch codifies official Austrian Standard German taught in schools and ministries.
units.regionalFocus: Nine federal states (Wien, Niederösterreich, Oberösterreich, Salzburg, Tirol, Vorarlberg, Kärnten, Steiermark, Burgenland) and signature greetings.

units.title: Travel Beyond the Guidebook: Wine Routes, Lakes & Thermal Spas
units.subtitle: Salzkammergut lakes, Wachau cycling, Therme wellness etiquette, and storytelling with temporal connectors
units.communicativeGoal: Narrate memorable travel experiences chronologically using bevor, nachdem, während, sobald, and seitdem.
units.grammarFocus: Temporal subordinating conjunctions—especially sequence-of-tense harmony with nachdem (Plusquamperfekt → Präteritum/Perfekt).
units.culturalNote: Central European sauna areas inside Thermen are traditionally textile-free quiet zones ('Ruhebereich — kein Schweiß aufs Holz!').
units.regionalFocus: Wachau Donauradweg, Salzkammergut Sommerfrische tradition, and Styrian Thermenland.

units.title: Media, Podcasts, Public Broadcasting (ORF / ARD) & Fact-Checking
units.subtitle: Summarizing audio reports, expressing agreement or skepticism, and quoting sources accurately
units.communicativeGoal: Follow German-language podcasts and evening news (Zeit im Bild / Tagesschau) and summarize stories to friends.
units.grammarFocus: Source attribution with laut + dative/genitive, zufolge (postposed!), and structured opinion frames (Meiner Ansicht nach...).
units.culturalNote: ORF's 'Zeit im Bild' (ZiB) at 7:30 PM and ARD's 'Tagesschau' at 8:00 PM are shared national touchstones.
units.regionalFocus: Ö1 radio documentaries, ZiB moderation style, and Austrian public-discourse vocabulary (Klubobmann, Nationalrat).

units.title: Debating Everyday Ethics: Mobility, Digital Privacy & Urban Living
units.subtitle: Structuring pros and cons, interrupting politely, and building consensus in group discussions
units.communicativeGoal: Hold your own in lively B1→B2 dinner or seminar debates on car-free city centers, cash vs. digital payments, and AI.
units.grammarFocus: Contrastive connectors (einerseits ... andererseits, zwar ... aber, im Gegensatz zu) and genitive noun chains.
units.culturalNote: Privacy awareness (Datenschutz) and valuing cash alongside cards remain deeply rooted civic instincts in Austria and Germany.
units.regionalFocus: Vienna's consistent #1 global livability rankings: social housing, 365-euro annual transit pass, and green-space planning.

units.title: Two-Part Connectors (Zweiteilige Konnektoren) & Rhetorical Flow
units.subtitle: Sowohl ... als auch, weder ... noch, nicht nur ... sondern auch, and je ... desto
units.communicativeGoal: Link complex ideas with crisp rhythmic balance in presentations, essays, and persuasive conversations.
units.grammarFocus: Correlative connector word order—especially verb-final 'je + comparative ..., desto/umso + comparative + V2'!
units.culturalNote: Well-structured correlative clauses give spoken arguments clarity without sounding academic or stiff.
units.regionalFocus: Discussing Austria's dual vocational apprenticeship & university education pathways (Lehre mit Matura).

units.title: Genitive Mastery & Formal Prepositions in Written Register
units.subtitle: Trotz, während, wegen, innerhalb, außerhalb, statt, and masculine/neuter -(e)s declension
units.communicativeGoal: Command crisp written and formal spoken German using high-register prepositions and clean genitive links.
units.grammarFocus: Genitive case across articles, adjectives, and N-declension nouns (des Studenten, des Kollegen, des Herzens) plus formal prepositions.
units.culturalNote: While casual speech famously swaps 'wegen dem Regen' (dative), confident B2/C1 writing and speeches shine with 'wegen des Regens'.
units.regionalFocus: Official Austrian administrative and journalistic genitive usage vs. relaxed Viennese dative speech.

units.title: Subjective Modal Verbs & Epistemic Nuance (Muss vs. Dürfte vs. Soll)
units.subtitle: Expressing 95% certainty ('Er muss im Zug sitzen') vs. cautious assumption ('Das dürfte stimmen') and hearsay ('Sie soll...')
units.communicativeGoal: Calibrate exact degrees of certainty, probability, and unverified rumor in professional and news discussions.
units.grammarFocus: Subjective modals in present and past (muss/dürfte/könnte/kann nicht + Partizip II + haben/sein) plus 'sollen' vs. 'wollen' claims.
units.culturalNote: 'Er soll reich sein' means 'People say he's rich'; 'Er will vor Ort gewesen sein' skeptically means 'He claims to have been there'!
units.regionalFocus: Austrian 'dürfte' as the polite journalistic favorite for cautious forecasts and estimates.

units.title: Passive Alternatives: Sich lassen, Sein + zu + Infinitiv & -bar Adjectives
units.subtitle: Saying 'Das lässt sich leicht lösen' and 'Das Problem ist kaum zu übersehen' like an idiomatic native
units.communicativeGoal: Replace heavy passive constructions with sleek, active-sounding German equivalents in meetings and writing.
units.grammarFocus: Modal passive substitutes: sich lassen + Inf., sein + zu + Inf., gehören + Partizip II, and productive -bar/-lich suffixes.
units.culturalNote: Native speakers prefer 'Das lässt sich einrichten!' ('That can easily be arranged!') 10-to-1 over 'Das kann eingerichtet werden'.
units.regionalFocus: Southern/Austrian 'Das gehört dringend repariert!' ('That urgently needs repairing!') construction.

units.title: Science, Climate, Alpine Glaciers & Clean Hydropower
units.subtitle: Nominal vs. verbal style: transforming dense noun phrases into clear spoken explanations and back
units.communicativeGoal: Read scientific and environmental journalism and present technical causes, consequences, and solutions fluently.
units.grammarFocus: Nominalstil ↔ Verbalstil conversion (Aufgrund des Anstiegs ↔ Weil ... angestiegen ist) and Future I/II conjectures.
units.culturalNote: Over three-quarters of Austria's electricity comes from renewable hydropower along the Danube and Alpine reservoirs.
units.regionalFocus: Alpine glacier monitoring (Pasterze am Großglockner), Nationalparks Austria, and Danube ecology.

units.title: Music, Visual Arts, Secession & Central European Cultural History
units.subtitle: From Mozart, Schubert & Mahler to Gustav Klimt, Loos, and contemporary Salzburg/Vienna stages
units.communicativeGoal: Discuss exhibitions, architectural movements, and musical performances with rich critical and historical vocabulary.
units.grammarFocus: Appositions in matching case, participial adjectives, and evaluative adverbs (bemerkenswert, wegweisend, umstritten).
units.culturalNote: The Vienna Secession's golden inscription—'Der Zeit ihre Kunst, der Kunst ihre Freiheit'—captures fin-de-siècle modernism in seven words.
units.regionalFocus: Wiener Moderne around 1900, Kunsthistorisches Museum, Albertina, and Salzburger Festspiele.

units.title: Business Negotiations, Project Proposals & Executive Presentations
units.subtitle: Structuring data-backed pitches, negotiating budgets and timelines, and summarizing action items
units.communicativeGoal: Lead a German-language client presentation, negotiate terms diplomatically, and write crisp protocol summaries.
units.grammarFocus: Concessive & conditional precision (sofern, vorausgesetzt dass, selbst wenn, ungeachtet + Gen.) and chart commentary verbs.
units.culturalNote: Punctuality, clear written agendas (Tagesordnung), and documented follow-ups build deep professional trust in DACH business culture.
units.regionalFocus: Navigating Vienna as an international headquarters bridge between Western and Central/Southeastern Europe.

units.title: Psychology, Communication & Navigating Conflict Constructively
units.subtitle: De-escalating misunderstandings, expressing empathy, and setting clear interpersonal boundaries
units.communicativeGoal: Address sensitive workplace or personal friction tactfully using 'I-statements' and nuanced modal framing.
units.grammarFocus: Subjunctive comparison 'als ob / als + Konjunktiv II' ('Er tut so, als wüsste er von nichts') and infinitive clauses with statt/ohne.
units.culturalNote: From Sigmund Freud and Viktor Frankl in Vienna to modern organizational coaching, German psychological vocabulary is unusually precise.
units.regionalFocus: Balancing German directness with Viennese diplomatic cushioning ('Ich würde meinen, dass...').

units.title: Contemporary Literature, Theatre & Film Across Austria, Germany & Switzerland
units.subtitle: Exploring DACH storytelling voices, stage dialogue, and film reviews
units.communicativeGoal: Read contemporary German-language novellas and critiques while appreciating stylistic voice across Vienna, Berlin, and Zurich.
units.grammarFocus: Free indirect speech (erlebte Rede), fronting for stylistic emphasis, and nuanced prefix pairs (durch·schauen vs. durchscháu·en).
units.culturalNote: Variable-stress verbs (úm·fahren 'knock over' vs. umfáh·ren 'drive around'!) reward attentive prosody.
units.regionalFocus: Vienna's Burgtheater ('die Burg') tradition and modern Austrian literary voices from Stefan Zweig and Ingeborg Bachmann onward.

units.title: B2 Capstone: Complex Argumentative Essays & Spontaneous Panel Debate
units.subtitle: Synthesizing multiple sources, steel-manning opposing views, and speaking coherently under time pressure
units.communicativeGoal: Deliver a structured 4-minute extemporaneous argument and write cohesive editorial-level German prose.
units.grammarFocus: Cohesion devices (darüber hinaus, demgegenüber, infolgedessen, nichtsdestotrotz) and tight clause architecture.
units.culturalNote: German academic and editorial style prizes Sachlichkeit—letting structured evidence carry persuasion rather than emotional exaggeration.
units.regionalFocus: Austrian Matura & ÖSD B2/C1 rhetorical expectations alongside Goethe-Zertifikat standards.

units.title: C1 Gateway: Extended Participial Attributes (Linksattribute) Unpacked
units.subtitle: Reading and crafting dense pre-nominal modifiers in law, journalism, rail, and scholarship
units.communicativeGoal: Parse four-line German noun brackets on the first pass in reading and listening, and deploy compact modifiers in formal writing.
units.grammarFocus: Present participle (Partizip I), past participle (Partizip II), and modal gerundive (zu + Partizip I: 'ein ernst zu nehmender Einwand').
units.culturalNote: The gerundive 'eine kaum zu überschätzende Bedeutung' compresses an entire modal passive relative clause into four crisp words.
units.regionalFocus: Unpacking official Austrian ministry, university, and ÖBB institutional prose effortlessly.

units.title: Konjunktiv I: Journalistic Neutrality & Indirect Discourse
units.subtitle: Reporting speeches, court testimony, and press conferences with er sei, sie habe, man werde
units.communicativeGoal: Read quality German-language newspapers with full sensitivity to speaker distance and report statements neutrally.
units.grammarFocus: Konjunktiv I formation across tenses (sei, habe, komme; sei gekommen, habe gesagt) and fallback to Konjunktiv II when forms collide.
units.culturalNote: Konjunktiv I does NOT signal doubt—it marks scrupulous journalistic neutrality that attributes claims cleanly to their speaker.
units.regionalFocus: Comparing Konjunktiv I reporting in ORF Zeit im Bild, Der Standard, Süddeutsche Zeitung, and NZZ.

units.title: Funktionsverbgefüge: Institutional & Academic Precision
units.subtitle: Zur Verfügung stellen, in Anspruch nehmen, in Frage stellen, and eine Entscheidung treffen
units.communicativeGoal: Upgrade plain B1 verbs into idiomatic C1 noun-verb collocations in professional reports, lectures, and correspondence.
units.grammarFocus: Productive light-verb constructions (bringen/kommen/stellen/ziehen/nehmen + prepositional noun) and negation placement before the PP.
units.culturalNote: Distinguishing 'in Frage kommen' ('to be a viable option') from 'in Frage stellen' ('to call into question') is hallmark C1 command.
units.regionalFocus: In Evidenz halten ('keep on file/mindful of') and urgenzieren / urgieren—distinctive high-register Austrian administrative verbs.

units.title: Derivational Prefix Mastery: Ver-, Zer-, Ent-, Er-, Be- & Miss-
units.subtitle: Multiplying your active C1 vocabulary 5× by feeling the semantic logic of verbal and nominal prefixes
units.communicativeGoal: Infer unfamiliar C1 words on sight and distinguish subtle cousins like erkennen, anerkennen, verkennen, and bekennen.
units.grammarFocus: Semantic patterns of inseparable prefixes (ent- removal/emergence, ver- transformation/error, zer- fragmentation, er- achievement).
units.culturalNote: A single root like 'stellen' yields vorstellen, einstellen, ausstellen, verstellen, erstellen, unterstellen, and bereitstellen!
units.regionalFocus: Austrian legal and administrative derivatives (angeloben, Kundmachung, Verlassenschaft, Pragmatisierung).

units.title: Economics, European Policy & Social Partnership (Sozialpartnerschaft)
units.subtitle: Macroeconomics, collective bargaining, fiscal debates, and reading central-bank & EU analyses
units.communicativeGoal: Engage fluently in executive and policy discussions on inflation, trade, energy transition, and labor models.
units.grammarFocus: Advanced causal/instrumental prepositions (angesichts, infolge, mangels, zwecks, anhand, zugunsten) + genitive.
units.culturalNote: Austria's post-war Sozialpartnerschaft brings chambers of labor, business, and agriculture together to negotiate consensus before strikes arise.
units.regionalFocus: Wirtschaftskammer (WKÖ), Arbeiterkammer (AK), Nationalbank commentary, and DACH economic terminology.

units.title: Law, Civic Institutions, Federalism & Officialese (Amtsdeutsch)
units.subtitle: Translating dense statutory and municipal letters into plain human action steps
units.communicativeGoal: Read tax notices, notary deeds, and civic ordinances with calm clarity without needing a translator.
units.grammarFocus: Unintroduced conditional clauses (verb-first 'Sollte die Frist verstreichen,...'), 'sofern nicht', and nominalized chains.
units.culturalNote: Fronting 'Sollte...' or 'Wäre...' in position 1 drops 'wenn' completely—creating sleek, high-register conditional elegance.
units.regionalFocus: Austrian civic terms: Bezirkshauptmannschaft, Magistrat, Bescheid, Erlagschein, and Bundes-Verfassungsgesetz.

units.title: Philosophy, Intellectual History & Essayistic German (Wissenschaftssprache)
units.subtitle: Reading Kant-to-Wittgenstein clarity, seminar discourse, hedging, and precision definitions
units.communicativeGoal: Follow university lectures, podcasts, and long-form essays in the humanities and sciences at native speed.
units.grammarFocus: Epistemic hedging (es liegt nahe, dass...; insofern ... als; es sei denn, dass...) and abstract noun formation (-heit/-keit/-ung/-ität).
units.culturalNote: Ludwig Wittgenstein's Viennese aphorism—'Die Grenzen meiner Sprache bedeuten die Grenzen meiner Welt'—celebrates crystal-clear thought.
units.regionalFocus: The Vienna Circle (Wiener Kreis), University of Vienna seminar traditions, and Austrian intellectual prose.

units.title: Wiener Schmäh, Cabaret (Kabarett), Irony & Register Play
units.subtitle: Decoding dry satire, understatement, double meanings, and classic Viennese & German Kabarett
units.communicativeGoal: Catch subtle irony, humor, and cultural allusions in live comedy, theatre, and witty dinner-party banter.
units.grammarFocus: Litotes ('nicht ganz unproblematisch'), rhetorical particles, ellipsis, and deliberate high/low register juxtaposition.
units.culturalNote: Political and social Kabarett in Vienna, Munich, and Berlin blends razor-sharp linguistic wordplay with affectionate self-irony.
units.regionalFocus: From Karl Kraus and Helmut Qualtinger to modern Austrian Kabarett—how Wiener Schmäh defuses tension with charm.

units.title: Idiomatic Mastery, Proverbs & Metaphorical Precision
units.subtitle: Deploying Redewendungen (auf den Punkt bringen, über seinen Schatten springen, den Nagel auf den Kopf treffen)
units.communicativeGoal: Use figurative idioms and proverbs with native accuracy, tone sensitivity, and effortless timing.
units.grammarFocus: Fixed syntactic idioms, metaphorical dative possessors ('Das liegt mir am Herzen'), and register-matched paraphrase.
units.culturalNote: Well-placed idioms make C1 speech vivid and memorable; overusing textbook proverbs back-to-back sounds unnatural—restraint wins.
units.regionalFocus: Beloved Austrian idioms: 'Das geht sich ums Arschlecken / haarscharf aus', 'Da fährt die Eisenbahn drüber!' ('No arguing with that!').

units.title: Crowning CEFR C1 Fluency: Pluricentric Command Across Vienna, Berlin & Zurich
units.subtitle: Effortless switching between warm Austrian regional authenticity, crisp Standard German, and literary prose
units.communicativeGoal: Speak, read, negotiate, joke, and write across any social, academic, or professional setting in the German-speaking world.
units.grammarFocus: Full-spectrum stylistic synthesis: cadence, register modulation, Konjunktiv I/II, participial elegance, and pluricentric awareness.
units.culturalNote: Mastery of pluricentric German means honoring local identity in Vienna, Salzburg, Munich, Berlin, or Zurich with equal grace.
units.regionalFocus: Complete command of Österreichisches Deutsch alongside Bundesdeutsch—knowing every nuance and feeling at home everywhere.
